source.title: REACT: Representational Early Analysis and Control of Chain-of-Thought Trajectories
source.authors: Han-Wen Zhang; En-Yi Jiang; Rui-Ke Zhu; Qi-Nan Yu; Sanmi Koyejo

record.tranche_reason: Tests one-shot addition of a learned safety direction at early reasoning positions and reports effects on harmful-request refusal and full-trajectory safety. The direction is initialized from a safe–unsafe mean difference but then optimized; it is not the original refusal-direction ablation applied across layers and positions.
record.gate_note: The study does not project out the direction, edit model weights, test jailbreak suppression, or use the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction. Position-sweep Safe rates are not direct refusal measurements; they are recorded as findings about full-trajectory safety, separate from the rubric-evaluator refusal rows. Probe AUROCs and gate-development statistics are not rows because they measure risk readability or routing performance, not refusal. The paper reports that benign-500 is not a broad capability benchmark.
record.test_reason: The paper adds a learned 'safety direction' once at an early CoT token (t2) of distilled reasoning models and reports its own method's results against CAST, AlphaSteer and prompt-boundary baselines. The direction contrasts paired safe vs. unsafe CoT trajectories, not harmful vs. harmless instructions. It starts from a mean difference but is then optimized with a signed continuation-NLL loss. It is applied at one layer and one position, and nothing is ablated or projected out. So no row measures the V1 object: the harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction, whose ablation removes and whose addition induces refusal. V8 asks whether V1 holds in reasoning models, so it is not tested either. The refusal increases describe the paper's own steering vector working as a defence. Arditi et al. is cited only in related work. These findings go under fits_no_version instead of verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors' central claim is that risk readability and causal controllability diverge. Later CoT states predict risk better but respond less to one-shot steering, so intervention sites must be chosen by their effect on generation. They avoid claiming that t2 universally beats prefill steering.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a safe-minus-unsafe mean-difference initialization from paired target-native CoT trajectories, then optimizes the direction for continuation likelihood and adds it once at a selected early-CoT state. It does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction or project it out across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on CoT position: 8B gains peak at t2 and are approximately absent at t3/t4; 1.5B and 7B windows shift by up to one token. Models use different layers and calibrated strengths. Prompt-boundary results depend on direction initialization. Gating changes benign refusal and trigger behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: A single learned safe-vs-unsafe trajectory direction added once at t2 raises rubric-judged refusal of harmful requests in three DeepSeek-R1 distills. On StrongREJECT: 1.5B 17.6→44.7%, 7B 31.1→73.3%, 8B 45.4→85.4%. Gains on the SORRY pool are smaller. Ungated, benign refusal roughly doubles; the gate restores it to baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In distilled reasoning models, a one-shot addition of an optimized safety direction at an early CoT token induces refusal of harmful requests, with a benign over-refusal cost when applied indiscriminately.

fits_no_version.finding: Effect of one-shot steering on full-trajectory Safe rate depends on CoT position. On 8B the gain peaks at t2 (+49.7 pp) and is about zero at t3/t4, even though later states predict risk better (AUROC 0.750 at t4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the evaluated distilled reasoning models, the effect of a single learned safety-direction addition depends strongly on intervention position, and readability of risk does not locate effective control sites.

record.problems: The direction-training and diagnostic pools are not fully held out from mean-difference initialization. The SORRY-derived evaluation shares source ecology with training. The main harmful safety metric uses automatic judging; rubric refusal results are single-seed. Benign-500 is an ordinary-instruction audit, not a hard-benign, mathematics, coding, knowledge, or complex-reasoning capability benchmark. The paper notes co-variation of model size, layer, and edit strength across models.
record.rows_left_out: Kept all Table 24 rubric-refusal rows, the three-seed main benign refusal/usefulness comparisons, and the position-sweep results that show the 8B early-window peak/collapse and cross-model t2 effect. Omitted the remaining Table 2 position rows for 1.5B and 7B (t0, t1, t3, t4); these are full-trajectory Safe rates rather than direct refusal measures, and the retained rows preserve the cross-model t2 result plus the decisive 8B positional contrast. Also omitted the 8B three-seed harmful Safe-rate comparison from Table 1 because the relevant t2 safety result is represented in Table 2 and direct refusal results are reported separately in Table 24.

untested.parts: No ablation or projection of any direction, and no harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction. The direction is added at one layer and one token, not every layer and position. No broad capability benchmark.
Does not test whether the original refusal direction mediates refusal in reasoning models. It only reports the effect of its own learned safety vector.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. (the original source) is cited only in related work. A cited 2026 paper argues CoT disrupts simple refusal steering, but this study does not test that. The direction is a safety/continuation-likelihood vector, not a refusal-mediating direction, so the rows are reclassified as fits_no_version rather than evidence on V1/V8. The Table 24 refusal rows are single-seed, rubric-judged (GPT-4o-mini/4o), with some fallback-judge cells.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the direction; does not add the original difference-in-means refusal direction at every layer and position; benign results are for ordinary instructions, not a broad capability benchmark.
Tests distilled reasoning models with the paper’s learned one-shot direction, not the original all-layer ablation or the original direction-extraction recipe.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Harmful-request refusal on StrongREJECT-273 for the three distilled reasoning models; t2 one-shot addition
reader_labels.reason: Rubric-evaluator refusal rises with steering in all three models; the 7B and 8B changes are especially large (ref15sr_steer, ref7sr_steer, ref8sr_steer).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SORRY-derived harmful set and benign instructions across the tested distilled reasoning models
reader_labels.reason: Refusal gains vary by set and model, while ungated additions raise benign refusal and reduce usefulness; gating largely returns benign outcomes to P0 (ref15so_steer, ref7so_steer, ref8so_steer, ref15ben_steer, ref7ben_steer, ref8ben_steer, ref15ben_react, ref7ben_react, ref8ben_react, ben8_steer_ref, ben8_react_ref, ben8_steer_use, ben8_react_use).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Distilled Qwen 7B and Llama 8B reasoning models on StrongREJECT-273; one-shot t2 addition
reader_labels.reason: The reported harmful-request refusal rates rise substantially after the edit in both reasoning models (ref7sr_steer, ref8sr_steer).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the three tested distilled reasoning models, including SORRY-derived and benign sets
reader_labels.reason: The size of the refusal increase varies across model and dataset, and ungated edits increase benign refusal; gate-controlled results stay near the benign P0 rates (ref15sr_steer, ref15so_steer, ref7so_steer, ref8so_steer, ref15ben_steer, ref7ben_steer, ref8ben_steer, ref15ben_react, ref7ben_react, ref8ben_react).
